label: D2 after choosing a1 (strongest when a1 commonly led to S1)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never D1/GO), and at D2 almost only when the trial choice was a1 (95.7% of a1 D2 steps active; 98% of activation mass). Magnitude is highest for a1 -> S1 common (about 0.8-1.0 of max), especially after a run of rewarded a1 choices with S1 good; intermediate for a1 -> S2 rare (about 0.3-0.55); the remaining weak activations (lowest quartile) are a2 -> S1 rare transitions (about 0.1-0.4). It does not fire on a2 -> S2 common, or on any D1/GO step. Adding the a2 -> S1 rare case, (phase==D2)&((in_action==1)|(in_state==1)), gives recall about 1.0 but lower precision, so F1 stays the same (0.911 vs 0.913). The simpler a1-choice predicate is recorded; it uses only observed inputs.

issues: Phase claims check out. On dev the feature is active on 0 of 380,619 D1 steps and 0 of 380,619 GO steps. All of its activation mass is at D2.
The a1-at-D2 claim checks out. Test scores: precision 0.953, recall 0.867, F1 0.908, mass recall 0.982. 95.7% of a1 D2 steps are active, and they carry 98.4% of the mass.

Magnitude ordering, checked against activation quartiles (test). a1->S1 common: precision 0.977, covers 100% of the top two quartiles, mass recall 0.85. a1->S2 rare: precision 0.88, sits only in quartiles 1-2, mass 0.13. a2->S1 rare: precision 0.46, sits almost entirely in the bottom quartile, mass 0.018. a2->S2 common: precision 0.0001, effectively silent. This matches the explanation's ordering.

Systematic miss class: a2->S1 rare at D2. About 45% of these steps fire, and they make up roughly 13% of active steps but only about 1.8% of the mass. The miss list on test consists almost entirely of this case. It fires more often when the previous choice was a1 (0.74 vs 0.43). The explanation states this case openly. Adding it gives test F1 0.909, about the same as 0.908, so it is a weak secondary component, not an unexplained gap.

False positives are about 11% of a1->S2 rare steps and about 2% of a1->S1 steps. Neither depends strongly on the good state (a1->S1: 0.987 when S1 is good vs 0.973 when S2 is good). This looks like a graded magnitude threshold, not a separate class.

Minor: the claim that magnitude is highest 'after a run of rewarded a1 choices while S1 is good' was not measured. The good state hardly changes how often the feature fires, so this part is unsupported, but it is a small embellishment.
The predicate uses only observed inputs (in_action at D2 is the observed choice), so there is no future-variable problem.
